title: Prove sharp arbitrary-term asymmetric cost on the named C5 core
body:
The asymmetric decoder handoff in PR2782 leaves open whether extra terms can lower the complete-plane pairing cost. This package proves **sharp cost 20 for any finite asymmetric decomposition over Q, R or C on the named physical C5 core `(13,23,35,16,34)`**. It complements PR3232's all-cycle Gram theorem and @petalas's PR3248 all-cycle five-term theorem; neither theorem is assumed here.

The written proof combines a weighted principal-block rank bound with equality traces. All 1,024 ordered support tariffs are reconstructed from authenticated physical geometry. Cost 18 is excluded by a trace obstruction; all ten possible cost-19 defect/count cases are excluded by exhaustive unbounded support-count reachability (4,872 states total). Repeated terms and zero-cost terms are accounted for. Five explicit cyclic terms attain 20 and fit the complete strict-scalar mask.

An independently written checker uses dense binary rank, rational Gaussian elimination and cost-layer enumeration instead of the primary pivot-rank, path-trace and BFS algorithms. Five behavioral control groups include a cost-19 support multiset that passes **all** principal rank counts but fails the necessary trace equations, signed asymmetric cancellation, loose-block handling, unbounded reuse and corrupted source bytes.

Validation on CPython 3.12.15:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c5-asymmetric-cost-floor` — primary proof receipt, independent reconstruction and optimized-mode controls pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/c5-asymmetric-cost-floor` — all 10 publication/source files match commit `1ea98246dabb46fc7bedf6127eff63f008414a39`.
- Metadata/source pins and `git diff --cached --check` pass. Canonical main and fork were synchronized; the branch is rebased on `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`.

Scope is one named core, ordinary transpose, and the inherited full source/target plane tariff. This is not an all-23-core or global decoder theorem, a native implementation, supplier admission or a new kappa. Selected cold replay and formal-kernel/human review were not run; the selected frontier is unchanged. The package records exact sources, predecessor credit and open next questions.

Canonical coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587#discussioncomment-19003119. Submission overlap covered 300 open PRs and 2,082 Discussion records with complete pagination; the complementary PR3248 scope is credited at its exact head.

Prepared by thakrarsagar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation, independent reconstruction, controls and review. Separate AI executions are not independent human review. Apache-2.0.
